summary.name: How to Avoid the 5 SRE Implementation Traps
summary.one_liner: A New Stack article that lays out five common pitfalls teams hit when adopting Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and the practices that help avoid them.
use_cases: planning an SRE rollout in an engineering organization
summary.what_it_does: The article describes five traps teams fall into when implementing SRE: lacking cross-team buy-in, having dense incident response processes, underusing postmortems, waiting for real incidents to train on, and stopping at incident management without SLOs. For each trap it suggests practices such as splitting incident command from a dedicated communications lead, using role-specific checklists, turning postmortems into searchable structured data, running simulated incidents or tabletop exercises, and treating SLOs and error budgets as the core of SRE. It is an opinion and best-practice piece rather than a description of a specific product.
notable: Covers five specific SRE adoption pitfalls with practical fixes
Explains error budgets as error budget = 1 - SLO
Recommends a dedicated communications lead during incidents, measured by stakeholder synchronization rather than resolution time
Cites Google's Coursera course on SLOs as a learning resource
caveats: Article is a general opinion piece and names no specific product that is being sold or reviewed
Some recommended 'ideal' systems are described generically rather than as available tools
Cost figure of $300,000 per hour for network downtime is attributed to Gartner as cited in the article
